source_text: ΠΕΡΙ ΕΥΧΑΡΙΣΤΙΑΣ, Λόγος. Ἠκούσατε τῶν ῥημάτων τοῦ Ἀποστόλου, δι' ὧν Θεσσαλονικεῦσι διαλέγεται, παντὶ νομοθετοῦντος τῷ βίῳ. Ἡ μὲν γὰρ διδασκαλία πρὸς τοὺς ἑκάστοτε αὐτῷ παρατυγχάνοντας ἦν· τὸ δὲ ἀπ' αὐτῆς ὠφέ λιμον ἐπὶ πᾶσαν διαβαίνει τὴν τῶν ἀνθρώπων ζωήν. Πάντοτε χαίρετε, φησίν· ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύχεσθε, ἐν παντὶ εὐχαριστεῖτε. Τί μὲν οὖν τὸ χαίρειν αὐτὸ, καὶ τί τὸ ἐξ αὐτοῦ ὠφέλιμον, καὶ πῶς δυνατὸν τὴν ἀδιάλειπτον προσευχὴν κατορθοῦν, καὶ τὴν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν εὐχαριστίαν ἀποδιδόναι τῷ Θεῷ, ὡς δυνα τὸν μικρὸν ὕστερον διηγησόμεθα. Ἅ γε μὴν παρὰ τῶν ἐναντίων ἡμῖν ἀπαντᾷ, διαβαλλόντων τὸ τῆς νομοθεσίας ἀδύνατον, ταῦτα προδιαλαβεῖν ἀναγκαῖον. Τίς γάρ ἐστιν ἀρετὴ, φησὶ, νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐν διαχύσει ψυχῆς φαιδρὸν καὶ γεγανωμένον διάγειν; Πῶς δὲ καὶ δυνατὸν κατορθωθῆναι τοῦτο, μυρίων περιισταμένων ἡμᾶς ἀβουλήτων κακῶν, ἀναγκαίαν τῇ ψυχῇ τὴν κατήφειαν ἐμποιούντων, ἐξ ὧν χαίρειν καὶ διευθυμεῖσθαι πλέον ἀδύνατον, ἢ τὸν ἀποτηγανιζόμενον μὴ ἀλγεῖν, καὶ τὸν κατακεντούμενον μὴ ὀδυνᾶσθαι; Ἤ πού τις καὶ τῶν περιεστώτων ἡμᾶς ἐνταῦθα, τὴν ἀσθένειαν ταύτην τῶν λογισμῶν ἀῤῥωστῶν, προφασίζεται προφάσεις ἐν ἁμαρτίαις, ὃς διὰ τὸ περὶ τὴν τήρησιν τῶν ἐντολῶν ὀκνηρὸν τῷ νομοθέτῃ περιτρέπειν τὰς μέμψεις ἐπιχειρεῖ, ὡς ἀδύνατα διορίζοντι. Καί φησι· Πῶς δυνα τόν μοι πάντοτε χαίρειν, τῶν αἰτιῶν τῆς χαρᾶς οὐκ ἐπ' ἐμοὶ κειμένων; Ἔξωθεν γάρ ἐστι τὰ ποιη τικὰ τοῦ χαίρειν, καὶ οὐκ ἐν ἡμῖν ἀποκείμενα· φίλου παρουσία, γονέων χρονία συντυχία, χρημάτων εὑρέ σεις, τιμαὶ παρὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, πρὸς ὑγείαν ἐκ χαλεπῆς ἀῤῥωστίας ἀποκατάστασις, ἡ λοιπὴ τοῦ βίου εὐημερία· οἶκος εὐθηνῶν διὰ πάντων, τράπεζα πλήθουσα, κοινωνοὶ τῆς εὐφροσύνης οἱ ἐπιτήδειοι, ἀκούσματα καὶ θεάματα ἡδονὴν φέροντα, ὑγεία τῶν οἰκειοτάτων, καὶ ἡ λοιπὴ αὐτοῖς τοῦ βίου εὔροια. Λυπηρὰ γὰρ οὐ τὰ ἡμῖν προσπίπτοντα μόνον τῶν ἀλγεινῶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰ φίλους καὶ συγγενεῖς ἀνιῶν τα. Ὥστε ἐκ πάντων τούτων ἀνάγκη ἀθροίζεσθαι τὸ περιχαρὲς καὶ εὔθυμον τῆς ψυχῆς. Καὶ πρὸς τού τοις, ὅταν ὁρᾷν ὑπάρχῃ ἐχθρῶν καταπτώσεις, ἐπι βούλων πληγὰς, εὐεργετῶν ἀμοιβὰς, καὶ ἁπαξαπλῶς ἐὰν μήτε παρόν τι τῶν δυσκόλων, μήτε προσδοκώ μενον ὅλως τὴν ζωὴν ἡμῶν ἐπιταράσσῃ· τότε δυ νατὸν ἐγγίνεσθαι τῇ ψυχῇ τὴν χαράν. Πῶς οὖν πρόσ ταγμα ἡμῖν δέδοται τὸ μὴ ἐκ προαιρέσεως κατορθούμενον, ἀλλ' ἐπακολούθημα ἑτέρων προηγουμένων ὑπάρχον; Πῶς δὲ καὶ ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύξομαι, τῶν τοῦ σώματος χρειῶν ἀναγκαίως τὴν ἔννοιαν τῆς ψυχῆς περιστρεφουσῶν πρὸς ἑαυτὰς, ἀδυνάτου ὄντος κατὰ ταυτὸν πρὸς δύο μερίμνας τὴν διάνοιαν κατα τέμνεσθαι; Ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν παντί μοι εὐχαριστεῖν διατέτακται. Εὐχαριστήσω στρεβλούμενος, αἰκιζόμενος, ἐπὶ τροχοῦ κατατεινόμενος, τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἐκκοπτόμενος; Εὐχαριστήσω τυπτόμενος τὴν ἄτιμον πληγὴν παρὰ τοῦ μισοῦντος; πηγνύμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ κρύους, λιμῷ καταγχόμενος, ἐπὶ τοῦ ξύλου δεδεμένος, ἀτεκνωθεὶς ἀθρόως, ἢ καὶ τῆς γυναικὸς αὐτῆς ἐστερημένος; ἐκ ναυαγίων ἐξαίφνης ἐκπεσὼν εὐπορίας; πειραταῖς κατὰ θάλασσαν, ἢ λῃσταῖς κατ' ἤπειρον περιτυχών; τραύματα ἔχων, συκοφαντούμενος, ἀλητεύων, τὸ δεσμωτήριον οἰκῶν; Ταῦτα καὶ ἔτι πλείω τούτων, κατηγοροῦντες τοῦ νομοθέτου, συνείρουσιν, ἀπολογίαν τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων ἑαυτοῖς εὐτρεπίζειν ἡγούμενοι τὴν ἐπὶ τοῖς διατεταγμένοις ἡμῖν, ὡς ἀδυνάτοις, διαβολήν.
thought_title: The Objectors' Case Against the Command to Rejoice Always
orientation: Basil has just begun his homily by quoting Paul's commands to the Thessalonians to rejoice always, pray without ceasing, and give thanks in everything, and now he turns to answer the objections of those who call these commands impossible.
pass_a_gloss: On Thanksgiving, a discourse. You heard the words of the Apostle, through which he speaks to the Thessalonians, laying down law for every life. For the teaching was for those who happened to be present with him at each time; but the benefit from it passes over to the whole life of human beings. Rejoice always, he says; pray without ceasing, in everything give thanks. What then rejoicing itself is, and what the benefit from it is, and how it is possible to achieve the unceasing prayer, and to render the thanksgiving in all things to God, as is possible, we will explain a little later. But the things that meet us from the opponents, who slander the impossibility of the legislation, these it is necessary to take up beforehand. For what virtue is it, he says, night and day in a pouring forth of soul to pass one's time bright and beaming? And how is it possible for this to be achieved, when countless unwilled evils surround us, producing necessary dejection in the soul, from which to rejoice and be of good cheer is more impossible than for the one being fried on a pan not to feel pain, and for the one being pierced through not to suffer anguish? Or perhaps someone of those standing around us here, being sick with this weakness of reasonings, makes excuses with pretexts in sins, who because of his sluggishness concerning the keeping of the commands attempts to turn the blame onto the lawgiver, as one ordaining impossible things. And he says: How is it possible for me to rejoice always, when the causes of joy do not lie in my power? For the things productive of rejoicing are from outside, and are not stored up in us: presence of a friend, long meeting with parents, discoveries of money, honors from human beings, restoration to health from a severe illness, the rest of life's prosperity; a house flourishing through all things, a table full, companions of good cheer who are suitable, sounds and sights bringing pleasure, health of those nearest, and the rest of life's smooth flow for them. For the painful things are not only the distressing things that fall upon us, but also the things that grieve friends and relatives. So that from all these things it is necessary that the very joyful and cheerful state of the soul be gathered. And in addition to these things, whenever it is possible to see the downfalls of enemies, blows of plotters, rewards of benefactors, and simply if neither anything difficult present nor expected at all disturbs our life; then it is possible for joy to come to be in the soul. How then has a command been given to us that is not achieved from choice, but exists as a consequence of other preceding things? And how shall I pray without ceasing, when the needs of the body necessarily turn the thought of the soul around to themselves, it being impossible at the same time to cut the mind into two cares? But also it has been ordered for me to give thanks in everything. Shall I give thanks while being tortured on the rack, while being maltreated, while being stretched on the wheel, while having my eyes gouged out? Shall I give thanks while being struck with the dishonorable blow by the one who hates me? while being frozen by the cold, while being choked by hunger, while being bound to the wood, while being made childless all at once, or also while being deprived of my very wife? while suddenly falling out of abundance through shipwrecks? while encountering pirates on the sea, or robbers on land? while having wounds, while being slandered, while wandering as a vagabond, while dwelling in prison? These things and still more than these, accusing the lawgiver, they string together, thinking that they are preparing for themselves a defense of their sins by the slander against the things ordered to us, as impossible.

choices.why: ἀποτηγανίζομαι refers to roasting or frying on a pan or gridiron, a specific torture; 'broken on the wheel' would be a different torture and mistranslates the verb.
ξύλον in a torture context means the cross or gibbet, not stocks; 'wood' preserves the literal sense without narrowing it to a specific instrument.

choices.english: in a pouring forth of soul
choices.why: διάχυσις means a diffusion or pouring forth; the objector uses it sarcastically of a relaxed, expansive state of soul, so the literal rendering keeps the metaphor.
rejected: in a relaxed state of soul

choices.why: ἄτιμος means dishonoring or dishonorable; the blow is one that brings dishonor, so the adjective is kept literally.
ἀλητεύω means to wander as a vagrant or homeless person; the rendering keeps the specific sense of aimless, destitute wandering.
εὐτρεπίζω means to make ready or prepare; the objectors think they are preparing a defense, so the literal sense is kept.

bible_refs.note: Πάντοτε χαίρετε, ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύχεσθε, ἐν παντὶ εὐχαριστεῖτε

pass_b_english: You have heard the words of the Apostle, in which he speaks to the Thessalonians, laying down law for all of life. His teaching was addressed to those who happened to be with him at the time, but the benefit from it extends to the whole of human life. “Rejoice always,” he says; “pray without ceasing; in everything give thanks” (1 Thessalonians 5:16-18). What rejoicing itself is, what benefit comes from it, how it is possible to achieve unceasing prayer, and how to render thanksgiving to God in all things—these we will explain a little later, as far as we can. But first we must deal with the objections that come against us from opponents, who slander the command as impossible. For what virtue is it, someone says, to pass night and day in a diffusion of soul, bright and beaming? And how can this be achieved, when countless unwanted evils surround us and force a necessary gloom upon the soul? Because of these, rejoicing and being in good spirits is no more possible than for a man being fried on a pan not to feel pain, or for a man being pierced through not to suffer. Perhaps someone here among us, sick with this weakness of reasoning, makes excuses in sins—one who, because he is sluggish about keeping the commands, tries to turn the blame onto the lawgiver, as if he were prescribing impossible things. And he says: How is it possible for me to rejoice always, when the causes of joy do not lie in my power? For the things that produce joy are external, not stored up within us: a friend's presence, prolonged time with parents, discoveries of money, honors from people, restoration to health from a severe illness, and the rest of life's prosperity—a house flourishing in every way, a table overflowing, close friends as partners in festivity, sounds and sights that bring pleasure, the health of those nearest to us, and the rest of their smooth course of life. For the things that grieve us are not only the painful events that fall on us, but also those that distress friends and relatives. So from all these things, the soul's overflowing joy and cheerfulness must necessarily be gathered. And in addition to these, when it is possible to see the downfall of enemies, the blows struck against plotters, requitals for one's benefactors—and, in a word, if nothing difficult is present or even expected to disturb our life at all—then joy can come into the soul. How then has a command been given to us that is not achieved by choice, but exists as a consequence of other things that come first? And how shall I pray without ceasing, when the needs of the body necessarily turn the mind's attention to themselves, since it is impossible for the understanding to be cut into two concerns at the same time? But I have also been ordered to give thanks in everything. Shall I give thanks while being tortured on the rack, while being abused, while stretched on the wheel, while having my eyes gouged out? Shall I give thanks while being struck with the dishonorable blow by one who hates me? While being frozen by cold, choked by hunger, bound to the stake, suddenly made childless, or deprived of my very wife? While suddenly cast out of prosperity by shipwreck? While falling in with pirates at sea or robbers on land? While having wounds, being falsely accused, wandering as a vagabond, living in prison? These things and still more they string together, accusing the lawgiver, thinking that they are preparing a defense for their own sins by slandering what has been commanded to us as impossible.

problems.why: χρονία means 'long-lasting/prolonged', not 'long-awaited'; the phrase means prolonged time with parents, not a meeting one has waited for.
problems.ruling: χρονία συντυχία means prolonged time with parents, not a 'long-awaited meeting'; meaning is changed.

problems.why: ξύλον in context of torture means 'cross' or 'stake', not generic 'wood'; this refers to crucifixion or similar execution.
problems.ruling: ξύλον in torture context means cross/stake; 'wood' loses crucifixion reference, misleading reader.

fixed: Changed 'a long-awaited meeting with parents' to 'prolonged time with parents' because χρονία means 'long-lasting/prolonged', not 'long-awaited'.
Changed 'bound to the wood' to 'bound to the stake' because ξύλον in this torture context means 'stake' or 'cross', not generic 'wood'.

problems.why: διάχυσις means diffusion/dissolution, not pouring forth; objectors mock ecstatic dissolution, not effusion.
περιχαρές is extreme/overflowing joy, not exultation; εὔθυμον is cheerfulness/high spirits.
εὐεργετῶν is genitive plural: of benefactors; ἀμοιβάς is repayments/requitals, meaning enemies' benefactors get repaid.
problems.ruling: εὐεργετῶν ἀμοιβάς = requitals of benefactors; 'rewards given to benefactors' reverses meaning—they are repaid, not rewarded.

edits.old: in a pouring forth of soul
the soul's exultation and good cheer
edits.new: the soul's overflowing joy and cheerfulness

fixed: Changed 'pouring forth of soul' to 'dissolving of soul' to match διάχυσις (diffusion/dissolution).
Changed 'exultation and good cheer' to 'overflowing joy and cheerfulness' to match περιχαρές (overflowing joy) and εὔθυμον (cheerfulness).
Changed 'rewards given to benefactors' to 'requitals of benefactors' to match εὐεργετῶν ἀμοιβάς (requitals of benefactors).

problems.why: διάχυσις means diffusion/spreading, not dissolving; 'dissolving' suggests destruction, opposite of joyful expansion.

ἀμοιβάς means requitals/returns, but context shows enemies' downfall; this means requitals *against* benefactors (i.e., bad things happening to one's enemies who were benefactors to others), or more likely 'requitals for benefactors' meaning good things happening to one's own benefactors. The English is ambiguous and likely wrong.

fixed: Changed 'a dissolving of soul' to 'a diffusion of soul': διάχυσις means diffusion/spreading, not dissolving.
Changed 'requitals of benefactors' to 'requitals for one's benefactors': ἀμοιβάς with εὐεργετῶν means requitals for benefactors, not requitals of benefactors.

dismissed.why: ἀμοιβαί means requitals/returns, but εὐεργετῶν is genitive plural, so 'requitals from benefactors' or 'requitals to benefactors', not 'for one's benefactors'.
dismissed.note: The genitive εὐεργετῶν is ambiguous, and in this list of things that bring joy, 'requitals for one's benefactors' is a fair reading.
